Technical Support www.analog.com  en-USFEATURES en-USFour 2 V rms differential inputs en-USOn-chip phase-locked looPLL\ for master clock en-USLow electromagnetic interference EMI\ design en-US109 dB analog-to-digital convertADC\ dynamic range  en-USTotal harmonic distortion + noTHD + N\95 dB  en-USSelectable digital high-pass filter en-US24-bit stereo ADC with 8 kHz to 192 kHz sample rates en-USDigital volume control with autoramp function en-USI2C/SPI controllable for flexibility en-USSoftware-controllable clickless mute en-USSoftware power-down en-USRight justified, left justified, I2S, and TDM modes en-USMaster and slave operation modes en-US40-lead LFCSP package en-USQualified for automotive applications en-USAPPLICATIONS en-USAutomotive audio systems en-USActive noise cancellation systems en-USGENERAL DESCRIPTION en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US incorporates four high performance, analog-to-digital converters ADCs\ with 2 V rms capable ac-coupled inputs. The ADCs use a multibit sigma--architecture with continuous time front end for low EMI. An I2C/serial peripheral interface SPI\ control port is included that allows a microcontroller to adjust volume and many other parameters. The en-USADAU1978en-US uses only a single 3.3 V supply. The part internally generates the required digital DVDD supply. The low power architecture reduces the power consumption. The en-USADAU1978en-US is available in a 40-lead LFCSP package. The on-chip PLL can derive the master clock from an external clock input or frame clock sample rate clock\ When fed with the frame clock, it eliminates the need for a separate high frequency master clock in the system.  en-USNote that throughout this data sheet, multifunction pins, such as SCL/CCLK, are referred to either by the entire pin name or by a single function of the pin, for example, CCLK, when only that function is relevant. en-USFUNCTIONAL BLOCK DIAGRAM en-US en-USFigure 1.  en-US

B | Page 12 of 44 en-USTHEORY OF OPERATION en-USOVERVIEW en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US incorporates four high performance ADCs and a phase-locked loop circuit for generating the necessary on-chip clock signals.  en-USPOWER SUPPLY AND VOLTAGE REFERENCE en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US requires a single 3.3 V power supply. Separate power supply input pins are provided for the analog and boost converter. Decouple these pins to AGND with 100 nF ceramic chip capacitors placed as close as possible to the pins to minimize noise pickup. A bulk aluminum electrolytic capacitor of at least 10 provided on the same PCB as the ADC. It is important that the analog supply be as clean as possible for best performance. en-USThe supply voltage for the digital corDVDD\generated using an internal low dropout regulator. The typical DVDD output is 1.8 V and must be decoupled using a 100 nF ceramic capacitor and a 10 µF capacitor. Place the 100 nF ceramic capacitor as close as possible to the DVDD pin. en-USThe voltage reference for the analog blocks is generated internally and output at the VREF pPin 2\ The typical voltage at the pin is 1.5 V with an AVDDx of 3.3 V. en-USAll digital inputs are compatible with TTL and CMOS levels. All outputs are driven from the IOVDD supply. The IOVDD can be in the 1.8 V to 3.3 V range. The IOVDD pin must be decoupled with a 100 nF capacitor placed as close to the IOVDD pin as possible. en-USThe ADC internal voltage reference is output from the VREF pin and must be decoupled using a 100 nF ceramic capacitor in parallel with a 10 µF capacitor. The VREF pin has limited current capability. The voltage reference is used as a reference to the ADC; therefore, it is recommended not to draw current from this pin for external circuits. When using this reference, use a noninverting amplifier buffer to provide a reference to other circuits in the application. en-USIn reset mode, the VREF pin is disabled to save power and is enabled only when the RST pin is pulled high. en-USPOWER-ON RESET SEQUENCE en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US requires that a single 3.3 V power supply be provided externally at the AVDDx pin. The part internally generates DVDD 1.8 V\ which is used for the digital core of the ADC. The DVDD supply output pin Pin 10\ provided to connect the decoupling capacitors to DGND. The typical recommended values for the decoupling capacitors are 100 nF in parallel with 10 µF. During a reset, the DVDD regulator is disabled to reduce power consumption. After the PD/RST Pin 6\ulled high, the part enables the DVDD regulator. However, the internal ADC and digital core reset is controlled by the internal POR signal power-on reset\ circuit, which monitors the DVDD level. Therefore, the device does not come out of a reset until DVDD reaches 1.2 V and the POR signal is released. The DVDD settling time depends on the charge-up time for the external capacitors and on the AVDDx ramp-up time. en-USThe PLL is enabled a fixed amount of time after the POR is released. Once the PLL is provided stable clocks it has a maximum lock time of 10mS in MCLK mode as mentioned in Table 5. Once the PLL is locked, its outputthe internal master clock\ivided and used to provide input clocks to the state machine. en-USThe state machine is also enabled for a fixed amount of time after the POR is released. Once the state machine has initialized, the ADC and other blocks become operational. The state machine initialization is not gated by PLL lock, only the state machine enable. PLL lock can occur after state machine enable with incorrect initialization configuration. In such cases, there is a risk of indeterminate ADC behavior for the en-USADAU1978en-US. One such instance where this could occur is if the input clocks to the PLL take a long time to stabilize. en-USFor proper initialization of the state machine, the software configuration needs to ensure that the en-USADAU1978en-US is not software-powered up until the PLL lock stabilizes. Thus, in MCLK mode the PWUP bitBit [0] of Register Address 0x00\an only be asserted at least 10 mS after DVDD > 1.2 V and the input clocks are stable. en-USPOR HYSTERESIS en-USThe internal power-on reset circuit is provided with hysteresis to ensure that a reset of the part is not initiated by an instantaneous glitch on DVDD. The typical trip points are 1.2 V with PD/RST high and 0.6 ±20%\h PD/RST low. This ensures the core is not reset until the DVDD level falls below the 0.6 V trip point.  en-USAs soon as the PD/RST pin is pulled high, the internal regulator starts charging up CEXT on the DVDD pin. The DVDD charge-up time is based on the output resistance of the regulator and the external decoupling capacitor. B | Page 16 of 44 en-USADC en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US contains four sigma-delta -channels configured as two stereo pairs with configurable differential/ single-ended inputs. The ADC can operate at a nominal sample rate of 32 kHz up to 192 kHz. The ADCs include on-board digital antialiasing filters with 79 dB stop-band attenuation and linear phase response. Digital outputs are supplied through two serial data output pins one for each stereo pair\ and a common frame clockLRCLK\bit clocBCLK\ernatively, one of the TDM modes can be used to support up to 16 channels on a single TDM data line. en-USWith smaller amplitude input signals, a 10-bit programmable digital gain compensation for an individual channel is provided to scale up the output word to full scale. Take care to avoid overcompensatiolarge gain compensation\, which leads to clipping and THD degradation in the ADC. en-USThe ADCs also have a dc offset calibration algorithm to null the systematic dc offset of the ADC. This feature is useful for dc measurement applications. en-USADC SUMMING MODES en-USThe four ADCs can be grouped into either a single stereo ADC or a single mono ADC to increase the SNR for the application. Two options are available: one option for summing two channels  of the ADC and another option for summing all four channels of the ADC. Summing is performed in the digital block.  en-US2-Channel Summing Mode en-USWhen the SUM_MODE bitBits[7:6] of Register 0x0E\e set to 01, the Channel 1 and Channel 2 ADC data are combined and output from the SDATAOUT1 pin. Similarly, the Channel 3 and Channel 4 ADC data are combined and output from the SDATAOUT2 pin. As a result, the SNR improves by 3 dB. For this mode, both Channel 1 and Channel 2 must be connected to the same input signal source. Similarly, Channel 3 and Channel 4 must be connected to the same input signal source. en-US en-USFigure 20. 2-Channel Summing Mode Connection Diagram en-US4-Channel Summing Mode en-USWhen the SUM_MODE BitBits[7:6] of Register 0x0E\e set to 10, the Channel 1 through Channel 4 ADC data are combined and output from the SDATAOUT1 pin. As a result, the SNR improves by 6 dB. For this mode, all four channels must be connected to the same input signal source. en-US en-USFigure 21. 4-Channel Summing Mode Connection Diagram en-US en-US en-US en-US en-US en-US en-US

B | Page 21 of 44 en-USCONTROL PORTS en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US control port allows two modes of operation, either 2-wire I2C mode or 4-wire SPI mode, that are used for setting the internal registers of the part. Both the I2C and SPI modes allow read and write capability of the registers. All the registers are eight bits wide. The registers start at Address 0x00 and end at Address 0x1A. en-USThe control port in both I2C and SPI modes is slave only and, therefore, requires the master in the system to operate. The registers can be accessed with or without the master clock to the part. However, to operate the PLL, serial audio ports, and boost converter, the master clock is necessary. en-USBy default, the en-USADAU1978en-US operates in I2C mode, but the part can be put into SPI mode by pulling the CLATCH pin low three times. en-USThe control port pins are multifunctional, depending on the mode in which the part is operating. en-USTable 11en-US describes the control port pin functions in both modes. en-US en-USTable 11. ADAU1978 Data Sheet  Rev. B | Page 22 of 44 en-USI2C MODE en-USThe en-USADAU1978en-US supports a 2-wire seI2C-compatible\bus protocol. Two pins, serial datSDA\ and serial clock SCL\, are used to communicate with the system I2C master controller. In I2C mode, the en-USADAU1978en-US is always a slave on the bus, meaning that it cannot initiate a data transfer. Each slave device on the I2C bus is recognized by a unique device address. The device address and R/W byte for the en-USADAU1978en-US are shown in en-USTable 12en-US. The address resides in the first seven bits of the I2C write. Bit 7 and Bit 6 of the I2C address for the en-USADAU1978en-US are set by the levels on the ADDR1 and ADDR0 pins. The LSB of the first I2C byte the R/W bit\ from the master identifies whether it is a read or write operation. Logic Level 1 in the LSB Bit 0\corresponds to a read operation, and Logic Level 0 corresponds to a write operation. en-USTable 12. VIL is the maximum voltage at Logic Level 0 that is, 0.4 V, as per the I2C specifications\ ISINK is the current sink capability of the I/O pin.  en-USThe SDA pin can sink 2 mA of current; therefore, the minimum value of RPULL UP  en-USDepending on the capacitance of the board, the speed of the bus can be restricted to meet the rise time and fall time specifications.  en-USFor fast mode with a bit rate time of around 1 Mbps, the rise time must be less than 550 ns. Use the following equation to determine whether the rise time specification can be met: en-USt = 0.8473 × RPULL UP × CBOARD en-USwhere CBOARD must be less than 236 pF to meet the 300 ns rise time requirement. en-USFor the SCL pin, the calculations depend on the current sink capability of the I2C master used in the system.  en-USAddressing en-USInitially, each device on the I2C bus is in an idle state and monitors the SDA and SCL lines for a start condition and the proper address. The I2C master initiates a data transfer by establishing a start condition, defined by a high-to-low transition on SDA while SCL remains high. This indicates that an address/data stream follows. All devices on the bus respond to the start condition and acquire the next eight bits from the master the 7-bit address plus the R/W bit\first. The master sends the 7-bit device address with the R/W bit to all the slaves on the bus. The device with the matching address responds by pulling the datSDA\low during the ninth clock pulse. This ninth bit is known as an acknowledge bit. All other devices withdraw from the bus at this point and return to the idle condition. en-USThe R/W bit determines the direction of the data. A Logic 0 on the LSB of the first byte means that the master is to write information to the slave, whereas a Logic 1 means that the master is to read information from the slave after writing the address and repeating the start address. A data transfer takes place until a master initiates a stop condition. A stop condition occurs when SDA transitions from low to high while SCL is held high. en-USStop and start conditions can be detected at any stage during the data transfer. If these conditions are asserted out of sequence during normal read and write operations, the en-USADAU1978en-US immediately jumps to the idle condition.  en-USFigure 33en-US and en-USFigure 34en-US use the following abbreviations: en-USACK = acknowledge en-USNo ACK = no acknowledge en-US en-US

Data Sheet ADAU1978  Rev. B | Page 25 of 44 en-USSPI MODE en-USBy default, the en-USADAU1978en-US is in I2C mode. To invoke SPI control mode, pull CLATCH low three times. This can be done by performing three dummy writes to the SPI port the en-USADAU1978en-US does not acknowledge these three writes, see fr-FRFigure fr-FR39en-US\Beginning with the fourth SPI write, data can be written to or read from the device. The en-USADAU1978en-US can be taken out of SPI mode only by a full reset initiated by power cycling the device. en-USThe SPI port uses a 4-wire interface, consisting of the CLATCH, CCLK, CIN, and COUT signals, and it is always a slave port. The CLATCH signal goes low at the beginning of a transaction and high at the end of a transaction. The CCLK signal latches COUT on a low-to-high transition. COUT data is shifted out of the en-USADAU1978en-US on the falling edge of CCLK and is clocked into a receiving device, such as a microcontroller, on the CCLK rising edge. The CIN signal carries the serial input data, and the COUT signal carries the serial output data. The COUT signal remains tristated until a read operation is requested. This allows direct connection to other SPI-compatible peripheral COUT ports for sharing the same system controller port. All SPI transactions have the same basic generic control word format, as shown in en-USTable 15en-US. A timing diagram is shown in en-USFigure 3en-US. Write all data MSB first. en-USChip Address R/W en-USThe LSB of the first byte of an SPI transaction is a R/W bit. This bit determines whether the communication is a read Logic Level 1\ or a writLogic Level 0\ This format is shown in en-USTable 13en-US. en-USTable 13.
